```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import inspect
import re
from math import comb

DOC = "PCP-006"
UO = "viral_inactivation"
UO_TITLE = "Low-pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ---------------------
_W = ["no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
      "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
      "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty"]


def w(n):
    """A small count in words, for running text."""
    n = int(n)
    return _W[n] if 0 <= n < len(_W) else f"{n:,}"


def g(v):
    return f"{float(v):g}"


def lc(name):
    return name if name.startswith("A-Mab") else name[0].lower() + name[1:]


def fv(v, unit):
    """A parameter value as the tables print it: pH to one decimal, anything else as given."""
    return f"{float(v):.1f}" if unit == "pH" else g(v)


def with_unit(v, unit):
    return f"pH {fv(v, unit)}" if unit == "pH" else f"{fv(v, unit)} {unit}"


def rng_u(lo, hi, unit):
    return f"pH {fv(lo, unit)}–{fv(hi, unit)}" if unit == "pH" else f"{fv(lo, unit)}–{fv(hi, unit)} {unit}"


def step_lc(k):
    n = T.STEP_NAME[k]
    return n if n.startswith("Protein A") else n[0].lower() + n[1:]


ver, eff = doc_version(DOC)
v1_date = rev1_date(DOC)
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
PCR = f"PCR-{uo.step:03d}"
PCP_PA = f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op('protein_a').step:03d}"
PCR_CEX = f"PCR-{CFG.unit_op('cex').step:03d}"
PCP_AEX = f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op('aex').step:03d}"
PCP_VF = f"PCP-{CFG.unit_op('virus_filtration').step:03d}"
scale_l = f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"
_order = list(CFG.train_order)
assert _order[_order.index(UO) - 1] == "protein_a" and _order[_order.index(UO) + 1] == "cex"

# --- parameters: the plan states the values its studies were planned against ------------
params = list(uo.parameters)
P = {p.key: p for p in params}
assert [p.name for p in params] == ["Inactivation pH", "Hold time", "Temperature", "A-Mab concentration"]
mv = [p for p in params if p.study == "multivariate"]
uv = [p for p in params if p.study != "multivariate"]
assert [p.key for p in mv] == list(D.rsm_factors(UO)) == list(D.screening_factors(UO)) == ["ph", "hold_time", "temperature"]
assert [p.key for p in uv] == ["protein_conc"]
n_par, k = len(params), len(mv)


def sp_char(p):
    return p.setpoint if p.setpoint_characterized is None else p.setpoint_characterized


def nor_char(p):
    return list(p.nor_characterized)


def nor_change(p):
    """How PCR-006 Version 2.0 changed the NOR: None, 'narrowed' or 'moved'."""
    a, b = [float(x) for x in nor_char(p)], [float(x) for x in p.nor]
    if a == b:
        return None
    if (b[1] - b[0]) < (a[1] - a[0]) and b[0] >= a[0] and b[1] <= a[1]:
        return "narrowed"
    return "moved"


sp_moved = [p for p in params if float(p.setpoint) != float(sp_char(p))]
nor_moved = [p for p in params if nor_change(p) == "moved"]
nor_narrowed = [p for p in params if nor_change(p) == "narrowed"]
assert sp_moved and nor_moved and nor_narrowed
changes_txt = (f"moved the set-point{'s' if len(sp_moved) > 1 else ''} of {join_and([lc(p.name) for p in sp_moved])}, "
               f"moved the NOR{'s' if len(nor_moved) > 1 else ''} of {join_and([lc(p.name) for p in nor_moved])} "
               f"and narrowed the NOR{'s' if len(nor_narrowed) > 1 else ''} of {join_and([lc(p.name) for p in nor_narrowed])}")

# range studied against the NOR as characterized (the sentences of the study design name them)
both_ends = [p.key for p in mv if p.prange[0] < nor_char(p)[0] and p.prange[1] > nor_char(p)[1]]
low_equal = [p.key for p in mv if float(p.prange[0]) == float(nor_char(p)[0]) and p.prange[1] > nor_char(p)[1]]
assert both_ends == ["ph", "temperature"] and low_equal == ["hold_time"]
assert [float(x) for x in uv[0].prange] == [float(x) for x in nor_char(uv[0])]

# the design centre is the midpoint of each range studied, not the set-point
centre = {p.key: (p.prange[0] + p.prange[1]) / 2 for p in mv}
assert all(float(centre[p.key]) != float(sp_char(p)) for p in mv)
centre_txt = join_and([with_unit(centre[p.key], p.unit) for p in mv])

# the parameter table: the values of plan_params(UO), with a note on each value PCR-006 Version 2.0 changed
_pp = plan_params(UO).reset_index(drop=True)
_letters = iter("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
_pnotes, _prows = [], []
_lmap = D.factor_letters(UO)
for _, _r in _pp.iterrows():
    _p = next(q for q in params if q.name == _r["Parameter"])
    assert float(_r["Set-point"]) == float(sp_char(_p))
    assert _r["Range studied"] == f"{g(_p.prange[0])}–{g(_p.prange[1])}"
    assert _r["NOR"] == f"{g(nor_char(_p)[0])}–{g(nor_char(_p)[1])}"
    _sp = fv(sp_char(_p), _p.unit)
    _nor = f"{fv(nor_char(_p)[0], _p.unit)}–{fv(nor_char(_p)[1], _p.unit)}"
    if float(_p.setpoint) != float(sp_char(_p)):
        _m = next(_letters) + ")"
        _sp += f" ^{_m}^"
        _pnotes.append((_m, f"{PCR} Version 2.0 moved the set-point to {with_unit(_p.setpoint, _p.unit)}."))
    if nor_change(_p):
        _m = next(_letters) + ")"
        _nor += f" ^{_m}^"
        _pnotes.append((_m, f"{PCR} Version 2.0 {nor_change(_p)} the NOR to {rng_u(_p.nor[0], _p.nor[1], _p.unit)}."))
    if [float(x) for x in _p.prange] == [float(x) for x in nor_char(_p)]:
        _m = next(_letters) + ")"
        _nor += f" ^{_m}^"
        _pnotes.append((_m, "The NOR equals the range studied."))
    _prows.append([_lmap.get(_p.key, "–"), _r["Parameter"], _r["Unit"], _sp,
                   f"{fv(_p.prange[0], _p.unit)}–{fv(_p.prange[1], _p.unit)}", _nor, _r["Study type"]])
tbl_params = T.frame(
    pd.DataFrame(_prows, columns=["Code", "Parameter", "Unit", "Planned set-point", "Range studied", "Planned NOR", "Study type"]),
    caption="Parameters of the low-pH viral inactivation step, with the set-points and NORs against which "
            "the studies were planned.",
    label="tbl-params",
    notes=_pnotes + [("", "Code, the letter of the factor in the design matrices of Appendices A and B. "
                          "A-Mab concentration is not a factor of the designs.")],
    notes_per_row=True,
    align=["l", "P{3.2cm}", "l", "r", "l", "l", "l"])

# --- designs ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
scr = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
rsm = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
c_scr, c_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
f_scr = int((scr.run_type == "factorial").sum())
f_rsm = int((rsm.run_type == "factorial").sum())
a_rsm = int((rsm.run_type == "axial").sum())
assert f_scr == 2 ** k and f_rsm == 2 ** k and a_rsm == 2 * k
assert f_scr + c_scr == n_scr and f_rsm + a_rsm + c_rsm == n_rsm
assert rsm[[f"coded_{f}" for f in D.rsm_factors(UO)]].abs().max().max() == 1
p_scr = 1 + k + comb(k, 2)
p_rsm = 1 + 2 * k + comb(k, 2)
dfr_scr, dfpe_scr = n_scr - p_scr, c_scr - 1
dflof_scr = dfr_scr - dfpe_scr
dfr_rsm, dfpe_rsm = n_rsm - p_rsm, c_rsm - 1
dflof_rsm = dfr_rsm - dfpe_rsm
assert dflof_scr > 0 and dflof_rsm > 0

# --- campaign thresholds (PCMP-001 Version 2.0) ----------------------------------------------
a_eff = g(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
a_lof = g(THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"])
gap_max = g(THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"])
ci_off_pct = g(100 * CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"]["offset_ci"])
cook_rsm = f"{4 / n_rsm:.2f}"         # the conventional Cook's distance cut-off 4/n, for the planned runs

# --- the NOR-propagated draw, as the engine makes it (doe_report._mc_predictive) ----------------
_nor_div = float(D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR)
sd_frac = "one " + {2: "half", 4: "quarter", 6: "sixth", 8: "eighth"}[int(_nor_div)]
n_sig = w(_nor_div / 2)
assert D.PI_LEVEL == 0.95                       # the central interval of the NOR-propagated analysis
mc_n = f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"
pi_pct = g(100 * D.PI_LEVEL)                  # prediction intervals of a single run or batch
vb_pct = g(100 * D.VERIFICATION_BOUND)        # the single-batch prediction bound of the verification of platform worst cases

# --- criteria for the step outputs (iac.csv) --------------------------------------------------
acc = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in ["aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf", "acidic_variants", "lmw_cesds_pct"]}
iac = D.iac_table(UO)
_all_iac = D.iac_table()
agg_hi = T.num(acc["aggregate_out_pct"][1])
frag_hi = T.num(acc["lmw_cesds_pct"][1])
acid_lo, acid_hi = T.num(acc["acidic_variants"][0], 1), T.num(acc["acidic_variants"][1], 1)
assert acc["acidic_variants"][2] == "two_sided"
claim = acc["xmulv_lrf"][0]
claim_txt = g(claim)
_agg = iac[iac.response == "aggregate_out_pct"].iloc[0]
agg_apriori = T.num(_agg["iac_high_apriori"])
assert bool(_agg["tightened"]) and not bool(_agg["widened"]) and _agg["iac_high"] < _agg["iac_high_apriori"]
assert set(iac[iac["tightened"] | iac["widened"]]["response"]) == {"aggregate_out_pct"}
_ver_all = D.iac_verification()
_tight = _ver_all[(_ver_all.cqa == "aggregates_hmw") & (_ver_all.met == False)]  # noqa: E712
assert list(_tight.step_key) == ["cex"]
_down = _all_iac[(_all_iac.step > uo.step) & _all_iac.cqa.isin(["aggregates_hmw", "fragments_lmw"])]
assert (_down[_down.step_key == "cex"].basis == "drug substance").all()   # nothing after cation exchange is credited
_frag = iac[iac.response == "lmw_cesds_pct"].iloc[0]
assert _frag["basis"] == "back-calculated"
assert float(_frag["downstream_fold"]) == float(_ver_all[(_ver_all.step_key == "cex") & (_ver_all.cqa == "fragments_lmw")].assumed.iloc[0])
assert iac[iac.response == "acidic_variants"].iloc[0]["basis"] == "drug substance"

# XMuLV claims of the train (PCMP-001 §7.4)
_xm = _all_iac[_all_iac.cqa == "lrv_xmulv"].sort_values("step")
xm_claims = {r.step_key: r.iac_low for r in _xm.itertuples()}
assert list(xm_claims) == ["viral_inactivation", "aex", "virus_filtration"]
assert float(xm_claims[UO]) == float(claim)
xm_sum = sum(xm_claims.values())
xm_req = float(_xm.iloc[0]["ds_low"])
xm_margin = xm_sum - xm_req
assert 0 <= xm_margin < min(xm_claims.values())
xm_steps_txt = join_and([step_lc(s) for s in xm_claims])

# Version 1.0 criteria for this step (INV-001)
_r1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO)
_r1_agg = _r1[_r1.response == "aggregate_out_pct"].iloc[0]
_r1_xm = _r1[_r1.response == "xmulv_lrf"].iloc[0]
agg_v1_margin = T.num(_r1_agg["margin"], 1)
assert _agg["iac_high"] > _r1_agg["high"]            # the Version 2.0 aggregate criterion is wider
assert claim > _r1_xm["low"]                           # the Version 2.0 XMuLV criterion is stricter
assert _r1_agg["rule"].startswith("nominal back") and _r1_xm["rule"].startswith("requirement")
assert set(_r1.response) == {"aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf"}

# platform worst cases this step verifies (PCMP-001 §7.5): the source strings are read, never retyped
_ver = D.iac_verification(UO)
assert set(_ver.assumption) == {"add_max"}
_short = {"aggregates_hmw": "Aggregate", "fragments_lmw": "Fragments", "acidic_variants": "Acidic variants"}
_wc_rows, _wc_notes, _mins, _wl = [], [], set(), iter("abcdefgh")
for _r in _ver.itertuples():
    _s = re.fullmatch(r"X/Y/Z-Mab low-pH hold, (\d+) min(.*)", _r.source)
    assert _s, _r.source
    _mins.add(int(_s.group(1)))
    _extra = _s.group(2).strip(" ;,")
    _ups = _all_iac[(_all_iac.cqa == _r.cqa) & (_all_iac.step < uo.step) & (_all_iac.basis != "drug substance")]
    assert len(_ups) >= 1
    _attr = T.ATTR_NAME[_r.cqa]
    if _extra:
        _mk = next(_wl) + ")"
        _attr += f"^{_mk}^"
        if _extra == "nrCE-SDS":
            _wc_notes.append((_mk, "Measured by nrCE-SDS."))
        elif _extra.startswith("A-Mab Table "):
            _wc_notes.append((_mk, f"The platform value also draws on {_extra.replace('A-Mab ', '')} of the A-Mab case study."))
        else:
            raise AssertionError(_extra)
    _wc_rows.append([_attr, T.num(_r.assumed),
                     join_and([f"{_short[_r.cqa]}, {step_lc(s)} output" for s in _ups.step_key])])
assert len(_mins) == 1
platform_hold_min = _mins.pop()
hold_nor_hi = g(nor_char(P["hold_time"])[1])
assert float(platform_hold_min) == float(P["hold_time"].prange[1]) > float(nor_char(P["hold_time"])[1])
assert float(P["hold_time"].nor[1]) == float(nor_char(P["hold_time"])[1])   # routine holds never exceed it
assert all(T.ATTR_NAME[c].endswith("(%)") for c in _ver.cqa)   # every increase is in %
tbl_wc = T.frame(
    pd.DataFrame(_wc_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Increase (%)", "Upstream criterion"]),
    caption="Platform worst cases of the low-pH viral inactivation step that criteria upstream of it rely on.",
    label="tbl-worst-cases", align=["P{4.4cm}", "r", "P{7.0cm}"],
    notes=_wc_notes + [("", f"Increase, the largest increase across the step for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, over a "
                            f"hold of {platform_hold_min} min.")],
    notes_per_row=True)

# --- the attributes in scope ----------------------------------------------------------
_cq_order = ["lrv_xmulv", "aggregates_hmw", "fragments_lmw", "acidic_variants"]
assert set(iac.cqa) == set(_cq_order)
_reg = cqa_reg.set_index("key")
assert _reg.loc["lrv_xmulv", "set_by"] == UO and list(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.set_by == UO].key) == ["lrv_xmulv"]
assert _reg.loc["aggregates_hmw", "set_by"] == "bioreactor" and _reg.loc["acidic_variants", "set_by"] == "bioreactor"
assert _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "set_by"] == "harvest"
assert _reg.loc["acidic_variants", "criticality"] == "VL" and _reg.loc["fragments_lmw", "criticality"] == "L"
# criticality follows the Tool #1 score for every attribute except viral clearance, which is very high by rule
_lvl = {"VL": 0, "L": 1, "L-M": 2, "M": 3, "M-H": 4, "H": 5, "VH": 6}
_nv = cqa_reg[~cqa_reg.key.str.startswith("lrv")].sort_values("tool1_score")
assert all(_lvl[a] <= _lvl[b] for a, b in zip(list(_nv.criticality), list(_nv.criticality)[1:]))
assert set(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key.str.startswith("lrv")].criticality) == {"VH"}
_cq = cqas_by_keys(_cq_order).reset_index(drop=True)
_lvl_name = {"VH": "very high", "H": "high", "M-H": "moderate to high", "M": "moderate",
             "L-M": "low to moderate", "L": "low", "VL": "very low"}
crit_legend = " ".join(f"{x}, {_lvl_name[x]}." for x in sorted(set(_cq["Criticality"]), key=lambda x: -_lvl[x]))
_cq_rows = []
for _i, _key in enumerate(_cq_order):
    _c = _cq.iloc[_i]
    _crit, _lv, _set = (_c["Acceptance"].replace("CEX/icIEF", "icIEF"), _c["Criticality"],
                        UNIT_OP_TITLES[_reg.loc[_key, "set_by"]])
    if _key == "lrv_xmulv":
        _crit, _lv, _set = _crit + "^a)^", _lv + "^b)^", _set + "^c)^"
    _cq_rows.append([_c["CQA"], _crit, _lv, str(int(_c["Tool #1"])), _set])
tbl_cqas = T.frame(
    pd.DataFrame(_cq_rows, columns=["Attribute", "DS criterion", "Criticality", "Tool #1", "Formed or set at"]),
    caption="Quality attributes in scope of this plan, from the drug substance CQA register.",
    label="tbl-cqas", align=["P{4.0cm}", "P{3.3cm}", "l", "r", "P{3.6cm}"],
    notes=[("a)", f"Cumulative requirement, met by the claims of {xm_steps_txt} together."),
           ("b)", "Very high by rule for viral clearance, whatever the Tool #1 score."),
           ("c)", "The register places the cumulative requirement at this step."),
           ("", "DS, drug substance. Tool #1, the score of impact multiplied by uncertainty (A-Mab case study). "
                + crit_legend)],
    notes_per_row=True)

# --- campaign facts -------------------------------------------------------------------
chron = csv("study_chronology.csv")
_plan_kinds = ["qualification", "screening", "rsm", "univariate", "hold", "retest"]
mine = chron[(chron.step == UO) & (chron.kind.isin(_plan_kinds))].copy()
assert sorted(mine.kind) == sorted(_plan_kinds)
sid = dict(zip(mine.kind, mine.id))
first_start = mine.start.min()
assert v1_date < first_start
assert mine[mine.kind.isin(["screening", "rsm", "hold"])].end.max() < AMD["date"]
assert mine[mine.kind == "retest"].start.iloc[0] > AMD["date"]
_mp = csv("method_plan.csv").set_index("study")
assert not _mp.loc[sid["screening"], "lmw_cesds"] and bool(_mp.loc[sid["rsm"], "lmw_cesds"])
assert bool(_mp.loc[sid["hold"], "lmw_cesds"]) and bool(_mp.loc[sid["hold"], "lmw_sec"]) and bool(_mp.loc[sid["rsm"], "lmw_sec"])
assert not _mp.loc[sid["qualification"], "lmw_in_scope"] and not _mp.loc[sid["univariate"], "lmw_in_scope"]
assert "CA2" in set(CAPA.id) and "fragment method" in CAPA[CAPA.id == "CA2"].iloc[0]["action"]

# scale-down qualification design
_q = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_q = _q[_q.step == UO]
n_sd = int((_q.scale == "scale-down").sum())
n_mfg = int((_q.scale == "manufacturing").sum())
_q_out = [c for c in _q.columns if c not in ("study", "step", "scale", "run") and _q[c].notna().any()]
assert sorted(_q_out) == ["acidic_variants", "aggregate_out_pct"]

# univariate design
_u = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
_u = _u[_u.step == UO]
assert set(_u.parameter) == {"protein_conc"}
u_levels = sorted(float(x) for x in _u.value.unique())
assert int(_u.replicate.max()) == 2 and len(_u) == 2 * len(u_levels)
_u_out = [c for c in _u.columns if c not in ("study", "step", "parameter", "level", "value", "replicate") and _u[c].notna().any()]
assert sorted(_u_out) == ["acidic_variants", "aggregate_out_pct"]
assert u_levels == [float(x) for x in uv[0].prange]
u_levels_txt = join_and([g(x) for x in u_levels])

# hold study design of the neutralized pool
_h = csv(f"hold_{UO}.csv")
hold_temps_txt = join_and(list(dict.fromkeys(_h.temperature)))
hold_days_txt = join_and(sorted(int(d) for d in _h.day.unique()))
hold_cesds_txt = join_and(sorted(int(d) for d in _h[_h.lmw_cesds_pct.notna()].day.unique()))
assert _h.hmw_pct.notna().all() and _h.acidic_pct.notna().all() and _h.lmw_sec_pct.notna().all()

# --- the tables of the methods, the sampling plan, the roles and the schedule ----------------
_amv = dict(AMV_REFS + VIRAL_INACT_AMV_REFS)
_meth = [["XMuLV log reduction factor", "Spiked load and neutralized pool", "AMV-3017"],
         ["Aggregate (HMW)", "Neutralized pool", "AMV-3011"],
         ["Fragments (LMW)", "Neutralized pool", "AMV-3020"],
         ["Acidic variants", "Neutralized pool", "AMV-3013"]]
assert all(m[2] in _amv for m in _meth)
tbl_methods = T.frame(
    pd.DataFrame([[m[0], m[1], _amv[m[2]], m[2]] for m in _meth],
                 columns=["Output", "Sample", "Method", "Validation"]),
    caption="Analytical methods for the outputs of the low-pH viral inactivation step.",
    label="tbl-methods", align=["P{4.0cm}", "P{3.6cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "l"])
_sops = dict(SOP_REFS)
assert all(s in _sops for s in ("SOP-3011", "SOP-3013", "SOP-3015"))
sop_list = VIRAL_INACT_SOP_REFS + [(s, _sops[s]) for s in ("SOP-3011", "SOP-3013", "SOP-3015")]

# --- planned design matrices (no results: a protocol shows the design only) --------------------
def planned_tbl(kind, label, caption):
    cm = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, kind, coded=True).reset_index(drop=True)
    nm = D.planned_matrix_df(UO, kind, coded=False).reset_index(drop=True)
    facs = D.rsm_factors(UO) if kind == "rsm" else D.screening_factors(UO)
    lmap = D.factor_letters(UO)
    # the run type is a column of its own with merged cells, never a heading row inside the body
    # (owner, 2026-10-09: "Do not mix grouping variables in tables as rows")
    tname = {"factorial": "Factorial", "axial": "Axial", "center": "Centre point"}

    def cfmt(v):
        v = int(v)
        return "0" if v == 0 else ("+1" if v > 0 else "−1")

    body, types = [], list(cm["Type"])
    for r in range(len(cm)):
        first = r == 0 or types[r] != types[r - 1]
        n = next((k for k in range(r, len(cm)) if types[k] != types[r]), len(cm)) - r
        body.append(([C(tname[types[r]], rs=n)] if first else [])
                    + [str(int(cm.loc[r, "Run"]))] + [cfmt(cm.loc[r, lmap[f]]) for f in facs]
                    + [fv(nm.loc[r, P[f].name], P[f].unit) for f in facs])
    head2 = [lmap[f] for f in facs] + [("pH" if P[f].unit == "pH" else f"{P[f].name} ({P[f].unit})") for f in facs]
    return CTable(header=[[C("Run type", rs=2), C("Run", rs=2), C("Coded level", cs=len(facs)),
                           C("Setting", cs=len(facs))], head2],
                  body=body, caption=caption, label=label, align="ll" + "r" * (2 * len(facs)),
                  notes=[("", " ".join(f"{lmap[f]}, {lc(P[f].name)}." for f in facs)),
                         ("", "The coded levels −1, 0 and +1 are the low end, the midpoint and the high end "
                              "of the range studied."),
                         ("", "Runs are listed in standard order. They are executed in random order.")],
                  notes_per_row=True)
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan sets out the Stage 1 characterization of the low-pH viral inactivation step, Step 6 of the A-Mab drug substance process [@fda2011; @amab2009]. It applies the Process Characterization Master Plan PCMP-001 to this step and adds what is specific to the step, which is its scale-down and spiking models, its designs, its sampling plan and the values of its criteria. The studies are run in a scale-down model at the development site in Cambridge, MA. Their results support the operating ranges and the control strategy that the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001 moves to the commercial drug substance facility in Grafton, WI. The commercial process runs at the `{python} scale_l` L scale.

Low-pH viral inactivation holds the Protein A eluate at acid pH for a set time and then neutralizes it. The hold inactivates enveloped viruses. The step contributes a log reduction of xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV) to the modular viral clearance claim of the process [@ichq5a]. The same conditions act on the antibody and can raise the levels of aggregate, fragments and acidic variants in the pool.

The plan covers the `{python} w(n_par)` parameters of the step, which are inactivation pH, hold time, temperature and A-Mab concentration. It covers the attributes that the step sets or can change, the scale-down model and its qualification, and the spiking model for XMuLV. It sets out the designed experiments, the univariate study and the hold study of the neutralized pool. It states the acceptance criteria and the planned analysis, including the proven acceptable ranges (PARs). The Protein A step that produces the load of this step is characterized under `{python} PCP_PA`. The results of this plan are reported in `{python} PCR`, which rolls up into the Process Characterization Master Report PCMR-001.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} v1_date`, before the first study of the step started on `{python} first_start`. Version 2.0 is a protocol amendment issued under the QA investigation INV-001. QA opened INV-001 on `{python} INV['opened']` after its review of PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed it on `{python} INV['closed']` with the classification `{python} INV['classification']`. The investigation found that the criteria used to judge each step in the PAR analysis were in no approved protocol and had been set after the data were seen (INV-001 finding 1). Corrective action CA2 of INV-001 amends each step plan with the criteria and the fragment method. This version is that amendment for Step 6, and it makes the following changes.

1. It sets out the intermediate acceptance criteria for the outputs of this step as PCMP-001 Version 2.0 derives them (@sec-iac). It also sets out the rule by which the verification of the platform worst cases may tighten or widen them (@sec-verification). The derivation uses no result of the studies in this plan.
2. It adds fragments as an output of the step and judges them on results by non-reduced capillary electrophoresis with sodium dodecyl sulfate (nrCE-SDS), following the method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD['date']` (@sec-methods). Size exclusion chromatography (SEC) reads fragments high in the Protein A eluate and in the neutralized pool (INV-001 finding 6).
3. It qualifies the scale-down model by its offset from manufacturing scale, and it states every judgement of an output with a known offset at manufacturing scale (@sec-sdm).
4. It judges XMuLV clearance at the least favourable combination of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature within their normal operating ranges (NORs), because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions (@sec-par). Version 1.0 judged XMuLV clearance on a single batch, as it judged the quality attributes.
5. It sets a criterion for the hold of the neutralized pool (@sec-hold-criterion).
6. It records the date on which Version 1.0 was approved. The title block of Version 1.0 carried `{python} REV1['effective']`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved. The revision history now gives the approval date of this plan (INV-001 finding 5).

@tbl-criteria-change compares the criteria that the Version 1.0 report applied to the outputs of this step with the criteria of this version.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.criteria_change([UO]).show()
```

The Version 1.0 aggregate limit was the drug substance criterion carried back through the nominal clearance of this campaign and divided by a margin of `{python} agg_v1_margin` (INV-001 finding 2). The Version 2.0 aggregate criterion is wider than that limit, and stricter than its own a priori value of `{python} agg_apriori` % HMW (@sec-iac). The Version 1.0 limit was never an approved criterion, because it was applied in the report at analysis and appeared in no approved plan. For XMuLV clearance, Version 1.0 subtracted the nominal clearance of the other steps in this campaign from the cumulative requirement. Version 2.0 holds the step to its platform claim, which is the stricter criterion.

The factors, ranges, NORs, set-points and designs are those of Version 1.0, against which the studies were planned and around which they were run. `{python} PCR` Version 2.0 `{python} changes_txt`. This plan does not adopt those values. The notes to @tbl-params give them and name `{python} PCR` as the document that made each change.

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The studies under this plan have the following objectives.

1. To quantify the effects of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature, and of their interactions, on XMuLV clearance, aggregate, fragments and acidic variants.
2. To fit response-surface models that predict these outputs over the range studied, and to test each model against the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2.
3. To determine, for each attribute that has a criterion at this step, the PAR of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature, and to establish whether the NOR of each lies within it.
4. To verify the platform worst cases of this step on which the criteria upstream of it rely.
5. To assess the effect of A-Mab concentration on aggregate and acidic variants one factor at a time, and to support its range against the criteria for those two attributes.
6. To establish how long the neutralized pool may be held before cation exchange.
7. To provide the evidence for the classification of each parameter under SOP-4001, and for the contribution of the step to the control strategy in PCMR-001.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

Low-pH viral inactivation is the step after Protein A capture and before cation exchange chromatography. The Protein A eluate leaves the column at low pH. It is adjusted to the inactivation pH and held for the hold time at the set temperature. Base is then added to neutralize the pool. The neutralized pool is the load of cation exchange. The step is operated under SOP-2009.

Low pH inactivates an enveloped virus by denaturing the glycoproteins of its envelope and by disrupting the envelope itself. The virus needs the envelope glycoproteins to bind to a cell and to fuse with its membrane. Inactivation follows first-order kinetics. Its rate constant rises as the pH falls and as the temperature rises, and the log reduction is proportional to that rate integrated over the hold time. Inactivation pH is expected to govern the step, because the envelope glycoproteins denature much faster with each small fall in pH near the operating range. A longer hold gives a larger log reduction at any pH and temperature, and a warmer hold speeds the denaturation of the envelope glycoproteins.

The same conditions act on the antibody. At acid pH the second constant domain of the heavy chain of the antibody is partially unfolded, which exposes hydrophobic surface. Molecules with exposed hydrophobic surface associate, so aggregate forms for as long as the pool is held at low pH. Aggregate forms faster in a warmer pool, because the unfolding and the association both speed up with temperature, and in a more concentrated pool (@sec-risk). On the platform, time at low pH adds a small amount of acidic variants. This plan measures that rise in every run of the designs, and `{python} PCR` verifies it against the platform worst case (@sec-verification). The low-pH hold also causes a small amount of acid-catalysed cleavage in the hinge region, which adds fragments. Over a hold of the length studied, the rise in acidic variants is expected to be small against the level formed in the production bioreactor, and the rise in fragments small against the level the load already carries. Aggregate formed in the hold is carried into cation exchange, the step that removes it.

The low-pH step belongs to the Novacyte downstream platform and was used for three earlier antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. Their history establishes the mechanism of the step and the range of performance to expect from it [@amab2009]. The same history supplies the platform claim for XMuLV clearance and the largest increases in aggregate, fragments and acidic variants that the step has shown. The intermediate acceptance criteria in @sec-iac are built on these values.

The step is not expected to change the glycan attributes, which are formed in the production bioreactor and which no downstream step changes (PCMP-001 §3). It makes no claim for the parvovirus minute virus of mice (MVM), because a parvovirus has no envelope and so no envelope glycoproteins for low pH to denature. The criteria also assume no change in host cell protein across the step, and no clearance of host cell protein is claimed for it.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

@tbl-cqas lists the attributes in scope of this plan, with their drug substance criteria and their criticality from the register of critical quality attributes (CQAs) in PCMP-001 §3. The register lists every attribute of the drug substance that has a criterion, whatever its criticality. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, as the product of impact and uncertainty [@amab2009]. For every attribute except viral clearance, a higher Tool #1 score gives an equal or higher level of criticality. XMuLV clearance was assigned very high criticality by rule, because a viral contamination would harm the patient directly, whatever its score (PCMP-001 §3). Attributes of high or very high criticality are called critical.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_cqas.show()
```

The step sets one attribute, XMuLV clearance. The requirement for XMuLV clearance is cumulative, and the step contributes its platform claim to it (@sec-claim). Aggregate and acidic variants are formed in the production bioreactor, and the register assigns fragments to harvest. The low-pH hold can add to each of these three attributes, so each has an intermediate acceptance criterion at the output of this step.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

Every parameter of this step was assessed in RA-001 before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on the CQAs and on its potential to interact with other parameters, as ICH Q9 describes [@ichq9]. RA-001 gives the scores and the rationale for each assignment.

Inactivation pH, hold time and temperature were assigned to multivariate study. A lower pH, a longer hold and a higher temperature each raise the log reduction of XMuLV, and each also raises the aggregate that forms in the hold. The three are also expected to interact. The log reduction is the product of a rate that pH and temperature set and the time over which that rate acts. A design that varies the three parameters together is therefore needed to estimate the clearance and the aggregate at their combinations.

A-Mab concentration was assigned to univariate study. A higher antibody concentration raises the rate at which partially unfolded molecules meet, so aggregate forms faster in a more concentrated pool. The mechanism of the step gives no reason to expect an effect of the antibody concentration on the inactivation of the virus, which acts on the viral envelope. This plan does not test that expectation, and @sec-risks lists it as an assumption. A-Mab concentration is also a property of the Protein A pool and not a setting of the hold. It is therefore assessed one factor at a time, for aggregate and acidic variants (@sec-univariate).

# Materials and methods {#sec-mm}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model holds the Protein A eluate in a temperature-controlled vessel at laboratory scale. The eluate is adjusted to the inactivation pH, held and neutralized in that vessel as in manufacture. The parameters of the step do not depend on scale. Inactivation pH, hold time, temperature and A-Mab concentration are therefore set to the same values as in manufacture, and the additions of acid and base are scaled with the volume of the pool.

The qualification runs are made under SOP-1001 in study `{python} sid['qualification']`, before the first characterization run. The study compares `{python} w(n_sd)` runs of the scale-down model at set-point with `{python} w(n_mfg)` manufacturing-scale batches, for aggregate and acidic variants in the neutralized pool. These runs give the offset of each of the two outputs. The decision whether the scale-down model is qualified for an output rests on whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, and that judgement needs the response-surface model. The decision is therefore made at the analysis, in `{python} PCR`.

The model is qualified for each output separately, by its offset from manufacturing scale and not by a test of equivalence (PCMP-001 §7.1). The rule has four parts.

1. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} ci_off_pct` % confidence interval.
2. Every scale-down result for aggregate or acidic variants is translated to manufacturing scale by subtracting the offset before it is compared with a criterion. Ranges and conclusions for these two outputs are therefore stated at manufacturing scale.
3. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval. The conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} w(k)` factors of the response-surface design.
4. A scale-down model whose conclusion for an output changes between the two ends of the confidence interval of the offset is not used for that output.

Where the cause of an offset is known, `{python} PCR` will state it.

Fragments and XMuLV clearance are not compared at both scales, so their offsets are unknown, not zero. These two outputs are judged as the model predicts them, with no translation to manufacturing scale. For fragments, representativeness rests on the mechanism of the step. Cleavage in the hinge region at low pH depends on pH, time and temperature, which the scale-down model sets to the manufacturing values, and not on the size of the vessel. The plan therefore assumes that the scale-down model forms fragments at the rate of manufacture (@sec-risks). For XMuLV clearance, representativeness rests on the spiking model.

Virus cannot be introduced into the manufacturing process, so XMuLV clearance is measured in a spiking model of the step [@ichq5a]. The spiking model is the scale-down model, run on the same Protein A eluate and at the same pH, hold time and temperature. Each run of the designs is spiked with XMuLV before the pH is adjusted. The XMuLV titre is measured in the spiked load and in the neutralized pool at the end of the hold. The inactivation rate depends on the pH and the temperature of the pool and on its matrix, which is the buffer of the Protein A eluate. It does not depend on the volume of the pool. The spiking runs use Protein A eluate produced at the set-points of the Protein A step, so the matrix is that of manufacture, and they hold A-Mab concentration at its set-point. The small-scale result therefore represents the manufacturing step at that concentration, provided that the whole pool reaches the inactivation pH. Whether the clearance changes across the range of A-Mab concentration is not tested, and the plan assumes that it does not (@sec-risks).

## Operation {#sec-operation}

Each run starts from Protein A eluate produced at the set-points of the Protein A step. The eluate is adjusted to the inactivation pH of the run and brought to the temperature of the run. The hold time is counted from the moment the inactivation pH is reached. At the end of the hold the pool is neutralized with base. Neutralization stops the inactivation and slows the reactions that the acid drives on the antibody. In the designs, A-Mab concentration is held at its set-point. In the univariate study it is set to each level before the pH is adjusted.

The acid and base solutions and the other inputs of the step are prepared to their platform specifications. They are controlled for identity and quality and are not characterized in this plan.

## Analytical methods {#sec-methods}

Each output is measured by a validated method under its own procedure. @tbl-methods lists the method for each output. SEC is run under SOP-3011, nrCE-SDS under SOP-3015 and imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF) under SOP-3013. The log reduction factor (LRF) for XMuLV is the reduction in log~10~ infectious virus between the spiked load and the neutralized pool.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_methods.show()
```

From the method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD['date']`, nrCE-SDS is the method for fragments wherever fragments are measured (PCMP-001 §7.8). Before that date fragments were measured by SEC, and SEC remains the method for aggregate. In the Protein A eluate and the neutralized pool, part of the host cell protein elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC and is counted as fragment. SEC therefore reads fragments high in the Protein A eluate and the neutralized pool (INV-001 finding 6). @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in which design. Aggregate was measured by SEC in both designs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study([UO]).show()
```

The screening design (`{python} sid['screening']`), the response-surface design (`{python} sid['rsm']`) and the hold study (`{python} sid['hold']`) ran before the method decision and measured fragments by SEC. The screening samples were not retained, so the screening design has SEC results for fragments only. These results are kept in the record and are not used for any decision. The retained samples of the response-surface design and of the hold study are tested by nrCE-SDS in the re-test study `{python} sid['retest']`, and fragments are judged on those results. The qualification study and the univariate study do not measure fragments.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

@tbl-sampling lists the runs of each study, the samples taken and the tests made on them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_sampling.show()
```

The centre points are replicate runs at the design centre. They give the pure error of each design, against which lack of fit is tested. The XMuLV titre is measured in the spiked load and in the neutralized pool of the same run, so that each run gives its own LRF.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

The designs and their analysis follow SOP-1002 and PCMP-001 §6. Each factor is coded −1 at the low end of its range studied, +1 at the high end and 0 at the midpoint [@montgomery2017]. An effect is the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, which is twice its coefficient in coded units. A model term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} a_eff`.

The screening data will be fitted by least squares with a model of main effects and two-factor interactions. For `{python} w(k)` factors this model has `{python} w(p_scr)` terms. The `{python} n_scr` runs of the design leave `{python} w(dfr_scr)` residual degrees of freedom. The `{python} w(c_scr)` centre points give `{python} w(dfpe_scr)` of them for pure error, and the other `{python} w(dflof_scr)` test lack of fit, which combines curvature and the three-factor interaction. The screening model identifies effects. Its centre points can detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor, and no prediction will be made from it.

The response-surface data will be fitted with a full quadratic model, which adds a squared term for each factor to the main effects and the two-factor interactions. The model has `{python} w(p_rsm)` terms. The `{python} n_rsm` runs of the design leave `{python} w(dfr_rsm)` residual degrees of freedom, `{python} w(dfpe_rsm)` for pure error from the `{python} w(c_rsm)` centre points and `{python} w(dflof_rsm)` for lack of fit. The response-surface model is the predictive model. Every prediction, every PAR and the verification of the platform worst cases in `{python} PCR` will come from it.

Each response-surface model will be reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², the model F-test and the lack-of-fit test against pure error. Predicted R² is computed from the prediction error sum of squares (PRESS), in which each run is predicted by the model fitted without it. Residuals will be plotted against the predicted values and the run order, and on a normal probability plot, and the Cook's distance of each run will be computed. The criteria that a model must meet, including the tests on its residuals, are in @sec-crit-models.

Aggregate, fragments and acidic variants must meet their criteria in every batch, and a response-surface model predicts the mean response. These three attributes are therefore judged through a `{python} pi_pct` % prediction interval of a single batch wherever a judgement supports a claim. Such judgements are the PAR computed while the other factors vary as in routine operation (@sec-par) and the judgement over the NOR in the qualification of the scale-down model (@sec-sdm), which uses the exact prediction interval of a single run. The PAR analysis that holds the other parameters at their set-points judges the mean prediction (PCMP-001 §6.4). XMuLV clearance is judged on the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable combination of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature within their NORs, because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions. Predictions of aggregate and acidic variants are translated to manufacturing scale by subtracting their offsets (@sec-sdm) before they are compared with a criterion. Predictions of fragments and XMuLV clearance are compared as the model gives them.

The results of the univariate study are compared with the set-point runs of the qualification study and with the criteria for aggregate and acidic variants in @tbl-iac. A difference from the set-point runs within the precision of the method is attributed to the assay. The hold study is evaluated as the change from day 0 at each temperature (@sec-hold-criterion).

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params lists the parameters of the step with their planned set-points and NORs and their ranges studied. The range studied is the characterized range of PCMP-001. The code letters identify the factors in the design matrices of Appendices A and B.

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_params.show()
```

For inactivation pH and temperature, the range studied extends beyond the NOR at both ends. It shows how the step behaves near and beyond the edges of routine operation, and it bounds the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed. For hold time, the range studied starts at the lower end of the NOR. That end is the shortest hold that the NOR of this plan allows, and the least favourable condition for XMuLV clearance. The range extends beyond the upper end of the NOR to show how aggregate and fragments grow in longer holds. For A-Mab concentration the NOR equals the range studied.

The centre of each design is the midpoint of the ranges studied, at `{python} centre_txt`. It is not the set-point of any of the `{python} w(k)` factors, because the ranges are not symmetrical about the set-points. The centre points therefore estimate pure error at the design centre. Each model predicts the outputs at the set-point from the fitted surface.

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening design (`{python} sid['screening']`) is a two-level full factorial design in inactivation pH, hold time and temperature, with `{python} w(c_scr)` centre points, in `{python} n_scr` runs. Every combination of the low and high ends of the `{python} w(k)` ranges is run, so the design estimates all main effects and all two-factor interactions without aliasing. Its purpose is to identify which factors and interactions act on each output before the response-surface design is run. All `{python} w(k)` factors are carried into the response-surface design, because each of them is expected to act on XMuLV clearance (@sec-risk). The runs are executed in random order. The planned design is in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface design (`{python} sid['rsm']`) is a face-centred central composite design in the same `{python} w(k)` factors [@montgomery2017]. It has `{python} w(f_rsm)` factorial runs, `{python} w(a_rsm)` axial runs and `{python} w(c_rsm)` centre points, `{python} n_rsm` runs in all. The axial runs lie at the centres of the faces of the design cube, at the ends of each range studied, so every run stays inside the range studied. Together with the centre points, the axial runs allow a squared term to be estimated for each factor, which the full quadratic model needs. The runs are executed in random order. The planned design is in Appendix B.

Every output in @tbl-methods is measured on every run. Fragments are judged on the nrCE-SDS results of the retained samples (@sec-methods).

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

A-Mab concentration is assessed one factor at a time in the univariate study (`{python} sid['univariate']`). The low-pH hold is run at the low and the high end of the range studied, `{python} u_levels_txt` g/L, in duplicate. Inactivation pH, hold time and temperature are held at their set-points. Aggregate and acidic variants are measured in the neutralized pool, and the set-point runs of the qualification study (`{python} sid['qualification']`) serve as the reference at set-point. The study does not measure XMuLV clearance or fragments, so it supports a range of A-Mab concentration for aggregate and acidic variants only. That A-Mab concentration does not change XMuLV clearance or fragments within the range studied is an assumption of this plan (@sec-risks). A study of one factor at a time cannot show whether the effect of A-Mab concentration depends on the other parameters.

## Hold study of the neutralized pool {#sec-hold}

The neutralized pool may be held before it is loaded onto cation exchange. During a hold, aggregate can form and asparagine residues can deamidate, which raises the acidic variants (PCMP-001 §5). The hold study (`{python} sid['hold']`) is run to establish how long the pool can be held. A neutralized pool produced at set-point is held at `{python} hold_temps_txt` and sampled on days `{python} hold_days_txt`. The design follows the hold study design that PCMP-001 §5 takes from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. Every sample is tested for aggregate and fragments by SEC and for acidic variants by icIEF. The hold study ran before the method decision AMD-001. Its samples of days `{python} hold_cesds_txt` were retained and tested for fragments by nrCE-SDS in the re-test study `{python} sid['retest']`, and the fragments of the hold study are judged on those days. The hold criterion is in @sec-hold-criterion.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

The criteria below apply PCMP-001 §7 to this step. They are derived from the drug substance criteria, the platform history of X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and the bounds of downstream steps verified on the data of this campaign (PCMP-001 §7.3 and §7.5). No result of the studies in this plan enters them. `{python} PCR` will report each result against its criterion and state whether the criterion was met.

## Scale-down model and model adequacy {#sec-crit-models}

1. The scale-down model is qualified for aggregate and for acidic variants when the conclusion against the criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} ci_off_pct` % confidence interval (@sec-sdm). The decision is made at the analysis, with the response-surface model.
2. A response-surface model is adequate for prediction when all four of the following conditions hold (PCMP-001 §7.2).
    - The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} a_eff`.
    - Lack of fit against pure error is not significant at α = `{python} a_lof`.
    - Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} gap_max`, the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2.
    - The residuals show no trend, and no run dominates the fit. A regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and a regression of the residuals on run order, each has no slope significant at α = `{python} a_eff`. No run has a Cook's distance above 4/n, where n is the number of runs in the fit (`{python} cook_rsm` for the `{python} n_rsm` runs of the response-surface design).
3. PCMP-001 §7.2 states that a model that fails the lack-of-fit test or the limit on overfitting is either refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or it is not used to set a range. This plan applies that rule to a model that fails any of the four conditions (the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test, the limit on overfitting and the tests on the residuals). The change is fixed here, before the data are seen, and one refit is allowed.
    - Where the regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values has a positive slope significant at α = `{python} a_eff`, the spread of the residuals grows with the level of the response. The response is then replaced by its logarithm, and the full quadratic model is fitted again.
    - Otherwise the terms that are not significant at α = `{python} a_eff` are removed one at a time, the least significant first, until every remaining term is significant or is needed to keep the model hierarchical. A model is hierarchical when every main effect contained in one of its interaction or squared terms stays in it.
    - A model that still fails any of the four conditions after this one refit sets no range. `{python} PCR` should then report the output against its criterion over the runs of the response-surface design.

## Intermediate acceptance criteria {#sec-iac}

A drug substance criterion does not say what the output of an upstream step must meet. Each output of this step is therefore judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion, as PCMP-001 §7.3 derives it. The drug substance criterion is carried backward through the train using the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform. That worst case is the lowest clearance factor for a step that removes the attribute, given as the clearance fold in @tbl-iac, and the largest increase for a step that adds to it. No margin is applied. An attribute that no downstream step changes keeps its drug substance criterion. @tbl-iac gives the criteria for the outputs of this step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation([UO]).show()
```

In @tbl-iac the downstream worst case is the cumulative clearance factor and increase of the steps after this one.

Aggregate in the neutralized pool must not exceed `{python} agg_hi` % HMW. Cation exchange is the only step after this one that is credited with removing aggregate, so the criterion is the drug substance criterion multiplied by the cation exchange clearance factor. Within its NOR, cation exchange cleared less aggregate than its platform worst case (`{python} PCR_CEX`). The one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of the clearance factor of a single cation exchange batch, at the least favourable combination within its NOR, therefore replaced the platform value (PCMP-001 §7.5). The a priori criterion of `{python} agg_apriori` % HMW tightened to the value in @tbl-iac.

Fragments in the neutralized pool must not exceed `{python} frag_hi` %, measured by nrCE-SDS. This criterion is the drug substance criterion carried back through the platform worst case of cation exchange, the only step after this one that is credited with removing fragments. Acidic variants must lie within `{python} acid_lo`–`{python} acid_hi` %, the drug substance criterion, because no downstream step is credited with a change in them. Both limits of the acidic variant criterion apply. XMuLV clearance must reach the platform claim of the step (@sec-claim).

## XMuLV clearance claim {#sec-claim}

Each step that clears a virus is held to its platform claim, which is the log reduction that the step has delivered for that virus on the platform (PCMP-001 §7.4). For XMuLV the claims are `{python} g(xm_claims['viral_inactivation'])` log~10~ for this step, `{python} g(xm_claims['aex'])` log~10~ for anion exchange and `{python} g(xm_claims['virus_filtration'])` log~10~ for virus filtration. They sum to `{python} f"{xm_sum:.2f}"` log~10~, which is `{python} f"{xm_margin:.2f}"` log~10~ above the cumulative requirement of `{python} g(xm_req)` log~10~. A shortfall at this step therefore cannot be made up by the claims of the other two steps. Anion exchange and virus filtration are characterized under `{python} PCP_AEX` and `{python} PCP_VF`, and PCMR-001 consolidates the cumulative claim.

The XMuLV clearance of this step is judged at the worst case within the NOR. The lowest mean predicted LRF among all combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature must reach `{python} claim_txt` log~10~.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-verification}

The criteria upstream of this step assume that the low-pH step adds no more aggregate, fragments and acidic variants than it added on the platform. @tbl-worst-cases lists these platform worst cases and the criteria upstream that rely on them. `{python} PCR` will check each of them with the response-surface model of this step (PCMP-001 §7.5).

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl_wc.show()
```

The verification of the platform worst cases takes the largest increase that the response-surface model predicts within the NOR of @tbl-params, at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. It also takes the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch at that combination. The bound is a prediction bound of a single batch because each output is judged per batch, and the platform worst case that it may replace was a single run. An assumption is confirmed when the predicted largest increase is no larger than the platform worst case. The results observed at the ends of the range studied are reported beside the predicted largest increase, for information.

The platform worst cases in @tbl-worst-cases are increases over a hold of `{python} platform_hold_min` min, the upper end of the range studied. The verification takes the A-Mab increase within the NOR, where the hold is at most `{python} hold_nor_hi` min. Where a bound replaces a platform value, the replacement therefore reflects the shorter hold and not a more stable product. The criterion that results is still right, because routine manufacture never holds the pool longer than the upper end of the NOR. The verification may change the criteria upstream of this step by the following rule.

1. Where the largest increase predicted within the NOR exceeds the platform worst case, the `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream of this step is recalculated with the bound and becomes stricter.
2. Where the `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch is smaller than the platform worst case, and the response-surface model meets the adequacy criteria of @sec-crit-models, the bound replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream of this step is recalculated with the bound and becomes wider.
3. Otherwise the platform value stands.

Where the rule widens a criterion, `{python} PCR` should give the argument for it, with the bound, the runs behind it and the reason why the performance of this step for A-Mab is known well enough to replace the platform value. Every change of a criterion, in either direction, should also be argued by its risk. The argument names who bears the risk, whether and where an excursion would be detected, what the downstream steps must then clear and the probability of a drug substance out of specification.

## Hold of the neutralized pool {#sec-hold-criterion}

The neutralized pool may be held at a temperature for as long as aggregate, fragments and acidic variants each meet the following criterion. The level that the pool is expected to carry in routine manufacture, plus the change measured over the hold, must meet the intermediate acceptance criterion of the pool in @tbl-iac. The criterion has four parts.

1. The expected level is the `{python} pi_pct` % prediction limit of a single run from the response-surface model, at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature. For aggregate and fragments it is the upper prediction limit. For acidic variants, whose criterion has two limits, the upper prediction limit is judged against the upper limit and the lower prediction limit against the lower limit.
2. For aggregate and acidic variants the expected level is stated at manufacturing scale, after the offset of @sec-sdm is subtracted. Fragments have no known offset, and their expected level is taken as the model predicts it, on the assumption that the scale-down model forms fragments at the rate of manufacture (@sec-risks).
3. Where no adequate model exists for an attribute, the most extreme result measured in the response-surface design on the side of the limit takes the place of the prediction limit.
4. The change is the result at the hold time minus the result on day 0 at the same temperature. Aggregate and acidic variants are judged on every sampling day. Fragments are judged on the days with an nrCE-SDS result, days `{python} hold_cesds_txt`.

`{python} PCR` will report, for each temperature, the longest hold among the days with an nrCE-SDS result at which every attribute meets this criterion, on that day and on every earlier sampling day.

## Parameter classification {#sec-class}

`{python} PCR` will classify each parameter by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.7, which reads as follows.

> Parameters are classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].
>
> 1. A critical process parameter (CPP) has an effect on a CQA that is significant and practically relevant within the characterized range, and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation.
> 2. A well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) has the same kind of effect on a CQA but a low risk of falling outside its acceptable range, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR.
> 3. A key process parameter (KPP) affects process performance, such as yield or concentration, and has no effect on a CQA within its range.
> 4. A general process parameter (GPP) has no relevant effect on a CQA or on process performance within its range.
>
> A significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical. The PCR-00N should state the size of the effect beside its significance and give the reason for each class.

An effect is significant when a term of the response-surface model that contains the parameter has a p-value below α = `{python} a_eff` (PCMP-001 §6.2). Criticality is treated as a continuum, as described in ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8].

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A PAR will be computed for each attribute that has a criterion at this step and for each factor of the response-surface model. Two analyses will be run (PCMP-001 §6.4). The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of interest across its range studied. Its PAR is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion.

The second analysis computes the PAR while the other `{python} w(k - 1)` factors of the response-surface model vary about their set-points as in routine operation. PCMP-001 §6.4 calls it the NOR-propagated analysis. It scans the parameter across `{python} D.PAR_GRID` grid points over its range studied. How the other factors vary, and what is compared with the criterion, depend on the attribute.

- For aggregate, fragments and acidic variants it compares the `{python} pi_pct` % prediction interval of a single batch, because a single batch is what must meet the criterion. At each grid point, `{python} mc_n` operating points are drawn for the other `{python} w(k - 1)` factors. Each factor is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of `{python} sd_frac` of the width of its NOR, so that the NOR spans `{python} n_sig` standard deviations on either side of the set-point. A draw that falls outside the range studied is set to the nearer end of that range. The interval holds the central `{python} pi_pct` % of the simulated batches, and it includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients. For an upper limit the upper end of the interval must not exceed the limit, for a lower limit the lower end must not fall below it, and for a two-sided criterion both apply.
- For XMuLV clearance it compares the worst case within the NOR. At each grid point the other `{python} w(k - 1)` factors are set to every combination of their NOR low, set-point and NOR high, and the lowest mean predicted LRF must reach the claim.

The PAR of the second analysis is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the comparison passes. It is in general narrower than the PAR of the first analysis, because the range must hold while the other factors vary. The PAR of the second analysis is the one that supports a claim. The decision rules are the following.

1. A range of a parameter is proven acceptable for an attribute when the second analysis meets the criterion of that attribute across it.
2. A parameter that affects several attributes has a PAR for each attribute, and the range carried into the control strategy is their intersection.
3. A PAR that reaches the end of the range studied is reported as reaching it, and no claim is made beyond it.
4. Where an output does not meet its criterion even at the set-point, `{python} PCR` reports that no PAR exists for that attribute and states the consequence for the NOR.
5. The range of A-Mab concentration is supported by its own univariate data for aggregate and acidic variants, the two attributes that the univariate study measures. It is supported when every result at both levels meets the criterion for aggregate and for acidic variants in @tbl-iac, at manufacturing scale. The univariate study supports no range of A-Mab concentration for fragments or XMuLV clearance (@sec-risks).

`{python} PCR` will tabulate both PARs for each attribute and each parameter. For each attribute it will also show a figure against the parameter with the largest main effect in the response-surface model. The figure plots the prediction across the range studied, with the region that meets the criterion shaded green.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

The data of these studies are recorded and kept to the ALCOA+ principles. Raw data from the analytical instruments and the scale-down systems are held in validated electronic systems with audit trails. Records made by hand are made on controlled forms. Every study record carries the execution window of the study and the calibration status of the equipment it used (INV-001 finding 5).

Results are transferred to the statistical analysis from the approved record, and a second analyst verifies the transfer. A result is excluded only for a documented reason, and `{python} PCR` lists every exclusion. Where a run is lost or invalidated, `{python} PCR` should report it and state whether the design was repaired or re-executed (PCMP-001 §6.1).

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-deliverables}

The deliverable of this plan is the paired Process Characterization Report `{python} PCR`. `{python} PCR` reports every study in @tbl-schedule against the criteria of @sec-criteria, and it rolls up into PCMR-001 with the reports of the other steps. The studies follow the sequence in @tbl-schedule. The qualification runs of the scale-down model are made before the first characterization run (PCMP-001 §5). The qualification decision needs the response-surface model, so it is made at the analysis, after the last study. The screening design is run before the response-surface design, so that its effects are known when the response-surface design is analysed. The re-test by nrCE-SDS follows the method decision AMD-001.

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The studies carry the following risks.

1. The scale-down model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale for aggregate and acidic variants. The offsets and the qualification rule of @sec-sdm address this, and every conclusion for these two outputs is stated at manufacturing scale.
2. Fragments and XMuLV clearance are not compared at both scales, so their offsets are unknown (@sec-sdm). Their judgements rest on the spiking model and on the assumptions below.
3. An infectivity titre carries the variability of a cell-based assay. The XMuLV claim is therefore judged on the mean prediction of the response-surface model and not on a single titre. The centre points estimate the variability of the LRF at the design centre.
4. The design centre is not the set-point (@sec-factors). The models predict the outputs at the set-point and do not measure them there. Replicate runs at set-point are made only in the qualification study.
5. The screening design has no fragment results that can be used for a decision (@sec-methods). Effects on fragments are therefore estimated from the response-surface design only.
6. The designs and the hold study need Protein A eluate produced at the Protein A set-points. A shortage of eluate would delay the studies, but it would not change the designs.

The plan rests on the following assumptions.

1. Each downstream step performs at least as well as the platform worst case on which the criteria of this step rely. Each such assumption is checked in the report of that step. The verification of the cation exchange aggregate clearance has already changed the aggregate criterion of this step. Cation exchange cleared less aggregate within its NOR than its platform worst case, and the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch for that clearance is part of the aggregate criterion (@sec-iac).
2. The step does not change the glycan attributes or host cell protein, and no credit is taken for either.
3. The scale-down model forms fragments at the rate of manufacture, because cleavage in the hinge region depends on pH, time and temperature and not on scale (@sec-sdm).
4. A-Mab concentration within its range studied does not change XMuLV clearance or the fragments formed in the hold. The designs hold A-Mab concentration at its set-point, and the univariate study measures neither output (@sec-univariate). For XMuLV clearance the mechanism of the step gives no reason to expect such an effect (@sec-risk). Cleavage in the hinge region is a reaction of each molecule with the solvent, so the fraction of fragments formed is not expected to depend on the antibody concentration either.
5. Each NOR spans the routine variation of its parameter, as the second PAR analysis assumes (@sec-par).
